exposure: Problems in CS delivery among friends and relatives
Possession of information concerning types of delivery
Presence of cesarean-related problems among relatives
outcome: Pregnant women's preferences for mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery or cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 402 pregnant women presenting to hospitals in Erzurum city center, Turkey.
finding: The proportion of cesarean delivery preferences was 17.2%, and women's preferences for normal vaginal delivery or cesarean sections were significantly affected by previous type of delivery, type of pregnancy, problems in cesarean delivery among friends and relatives, cesarean section experience, and educational status.
mod_finding: Pregnant women's preferences for mode of birth (NVD or CS) were significantly affected by previous type of delivery, type of pregnancy (natural vs. assisted), problems in CS delivery among friends and relatives, cesarean section experience, and educational status.
